# 07 Close the board: the numbers, the policy, and what is next

## Outcome

The compatibility position is written where the next planner will read it, with the numbers this
board actually produced rather than the ones it started from.

## Why this ticket exists

This board's deliverable is half instrument and half fix, and the instrument is worthless if
nobody knows it exists. It also leaves the numbers in a shape that needs explaining: `rejected`
went **up** before it went down, on purpose.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `CONTEXT.md` gains **Compatibility corpus** as a term: what the three states mean, that
      `silently-wrong` must be zero, that `rejected` may only shrink, and that a `supported` entry
      must assert meaning. Mind the existing `_Avoid_` lines.
- [x] `CONTEXT.md` states the policy in one sentence an author or a maintainer can act on:
      **while a construct is unimplemented, Siren rejects it rather than rendering it wrongly.**
- [x] `.dev/mermaid-compatibility-gaps.md` is updated to the board's final numbers, with the
      before/after for each of the three kinds, and a note that the document is now a *narrative*
      — the corpus is the authority, and a future reader should trust the test over the prose.
- [x] `.dev/mermaid-diagram-roadmap.md` marks this board done, names the remaining gaps in the
      order the spec's non-goals put them (node shapes, edge forms, subgraph, click, accTitle,
      sequence's five, the class lollipop), and says which are contract changes and which are not.
- [x] An example demonstrates what landed: a flowchart using `graph`, a chained edge, `&`, and a
      quoted label, rendering with **zero diagnostics**. Check whether an existing example should
      grow it rather than adding a file — say which you chose and why.
- [x] **The ratchet numbers in `corpus.test.ts` are the ones the suite actually produces**, and
      your report states them alongside the board's starting numbers. If any case is still
      `silently-wrong`, name it and say why it survived — the spec says that count reaches zero,
      and a board that did not get there should say so out loud rather than quietly.

- [x] **Carried from ticket 03, and needs a source outside this repo.** The corpus row for
      `seq-activation-shorthand` says "`+` activates the target's lifeline and `-` deactivates it".
      Mermaid's canonical example is `Alice->>+John: …` then `John-->>-Alice: …`, where the `-`
      appears to deactivate **John** — the *sender* of that message, not its target. Neither the
      ticket-03 worker nor the integrator could settle it from anything in this repo, and both
      declined to correct it from memory. Settle it against real Mermaid and fix the prose, or say
      plainly in the row that it is unverified. Do not guess.

- [x] **Found by ticket 04.** `parseSequenceDiagram` and `parseClassDiagram` still write their own
      header diagnostics rather than going through `listAcceptedHeaders`. No drift today — each
      names only its own kind — but flowchart just gained an alias, and the moment another kind
      does, that is the second list the helper exists to prevent. Record it in the roadmap as a
      known shape, or fix it if it is genuinely one line; say which.

- [x] **Give the Mermaid probe a permanent home.** Ticket 05 installed mermaid 11.17.2 in the
      session scratchpad and drove its `FlowDB` + jison parser under jsdom to settle three
      questions in minutes that would otherwise have been guesses — edge ordering, chain
      composition, and `;` semantics — and it is about to be lost. Every future compatibility board
      has the same kind of question, and the spec's decision 6 now *requires* Mermaid's behavior to
      be measured rather than remembered, so this is no longer a convenience.
      Decide where it lives and say why: a committed dev script with `mermaid` as a devDependency
      is the obvious answer, but `.dev/` is gitignored and would lose it on a fresh clone, so a
      recipe there is not enough. Adding the dependency is authorized.

- [x] **Found by ticket 06, measured.** Mermaid trims label whitespace and Siren does not:
      `A[  x  ]` and `A["  x  "]` are both `x` in mermaid 11.17.2 and both `  x  ` here. It
      predates this board and is uniform across quoted and unquoted labels — ticket 06 left it
      uniform rather than fixing half of it. `A["  x  "]` is valid Mermaid, so this is a real
      compat gap: give it a corpus row (`silently-wrong`, since it renders with no diagnostic and
      the wrong text) or record it in the roadmap. Say which, and if you add the row, the ratchet
      moves and the reason is "a measurement was corrected", not "code got worse".

## Status

Done (2026-09-07), commit 1ef616a. 3 slices (2 red-green plus a self-caught weak-test slice),
with the prose and tooling items declared as having no honest red-green pair.

707 core tests / 29 board, tsc clean both, both build. Final corpus: **32 / 33 / 3**.

Slice 1b is worth noting: the example test's red was existence-level, so the worker checked whether
it discriminated by rewriting the example longhand — it stayed green. It then added an assertion on
the example's own text, because otherwise nothing would stop the repo losing its only example of
this syntax.
